clock_time_reference: The Democracy Clock closed the week at 7:43 p.m., the same public time at which it began, reflecting a net movement of roughly two-tenths of a minute backward. The near-stillness of the number conceals significant churn between offsetting negative and positive developments.

delta_summary.moral_floor: Severe and steady-state: entrenched abuses in war-making, retaliation, and oversight evasion persisted without sharp new escalation, held level by scattered but real judicial and legislative resistance.
delta_summary.net_interpretation: Week 65 reads as consolidation rather than acceleration. The tools of unchecked executive power, retaliation against watchdogs, and federal funding coercion were reused rather than expanded into new categories, while a disbarment, a construction injunction, two resignations, and a bipartisan immigration bill held the line without reversing the underlying trend.

traits_moved.note: Twenty-one traits registered movement this week, with negative shifts in war powers, whistleblower protection, and judicial independence partially offset by positive movement in opposition capacity.

long_synopsis: Week 65 opened with a presidential blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, ordered without congressional authorization, and closed with an unverified declaration of victory contradicted by Iranian officials. In between, the administration fired judges who ruled against it, issued criminal referrals against a whistleblower and the inspector general who processed his complaint, and moved to erase January 6 seditious conspiracy convictions. Congress narrowly failed to check the war powers, 214-213, but passed bipartisan Haitian protections and forced two ethics resignations. Courts disbarred a fake-elector architect and halted a White House construction project. Inflation and gas prices rose on war-linked costs. Trump posted, then deleted, AI images of himself as Jesus, while attacking the Pope. The clock moved two-tenths of a minute backward, holding nearly level under sustained pressure.
short_synopsis: An unauthorized blockade, a false victory claim, retaliation against a whistleblower and inspector general, and religious self-glorification defined the week, while narrow congressional votes, a disbarment, and a construction injunction held the clock nearly level.

subtitle: A week of unchecked war powers, whistleblower retaliation, and religious spectacle ends where it began, held level only by scattered resistance.
tagline: The republic didn't fall this week. It just kept absorbing blows, one narrow vote and one lonely judge at a time.
